newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. welcomes Nobel award to East Timor campaigners.
newsitem.headline: U.N. welcomes Nobel award to East Timor campaigners.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali congratulated the two East Timor rights activists who won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday and said he hoped the award would have a positive effect on efforts to resolve the East Timor issue.

The $1.2-million prize went to Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo, Roman Catholic Bishop of Dili, East Timor's capital, and exiled resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta for their efforts aimed at a peaceful solution to the conflict in the former Portuguese colony annexed by Indonesia in 1976.
Welcoming the award, Boutros-Ghali said in a statement he hoped it would "positively affect the continuing negotiations in the search for a lasting settlement."

Recalling that the U.N. secretary-general had been working to resolve the issue since 1983, he said: "In this capacity he has had the opportunity to consult on various occasions with Bishop Belo whose wisdom and commitment to peace and human rights has won him the respect of his people and of the international community.

"Both Bishop Belo and Mr Ramos-Horta have participated actively in the all-inclusive intra-East Timorese dialogue facilitated by the secretary-general," he added, referring to meetings in Austria attended by representatives from inside and outside the territory.
